messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Pager: eng-oncall — High tail latency + 5xx spike affecting /v1/generate (service=runtime, metric=token_latency_95, alert=KV_CACHE_BLOWUP). Alert triggered at 2026-03-15T02:32:02Z. Initial severity: P1.

maya (oncall): seeing the pager. 95p tok latency up to ~1.8s and 500s for some traces. Autoscales flapping.

jonah (sre): adding context: last deploy was a batching config tweak at 02:10 that enabled continuous batching warmup on a 2s window. HPA activity shows rapid scale-ups and downs since ~02:20.

kevin (runtime): probable root: KV prefix cache growth when warmup batches hit many unique prefixes. Cache eviction not keeping up -> memory-backed thrash + slower kernel selection -> huge p95.

maya (oncall): customer impact: multiple production customers in EU seeing timeouts; some requests retried by clients causing doubled traffic. Carla can you surface any priority customers?

carla (support): confirmed: two enterprise customers (AcmeHealth, BlueBooks) reported elevated errors around 02:30. Support ticket numbers: #2841, #2845. Both flagged "severe".

priya (prod-eng): immediate mitigations we can try: 1) revert the continuous-batching warmup flag; 2) reduce batch size cap to 64; 3) bump cache eviction aggressiveness (TTL -> 30s). Which is least risky to roll now?

jonah (sre): least risky = config flip for warmup flag. We can toggle via feature flag in runtime without full deploy. I'll prepare the rollback command.

zack (eng-infra): watch HPA: the thrash is driven by CPU probe spikes from batching. HPA min=4 max=20; current oscillation 6 <-> 18. We might temporarily increase min=8 to stabilize while we fix. Would prefer to avoid higher long-term cost.

maya (oncall): i'm going to open a mitigation runbook and handoff if needed. tagging kevin and jonah for rollout.

kevin (runtime): crafting flag flip now. command: 

```
# Flip continuous-batching warmup to off
curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN" \
  https://control-plane/api/v1/runtime/flags/continuous_batching_warmup -d '{"enabled":false}'
```

kevin (runtime): executing in 1m. will watch error rates and p95.

ops-bot: Running change: flag_toggle by kevin. Change-id: ch-20260315-001. Starting rollout to runtime-pools: us-east-1, eu-west-1.

jonah (sre): while that's rolling, I'm patching HPA to add 120s stabilization window and bump min to 8:

```
kubectl patch hpa runtime-hpa -n production --type='merge' -p '{"spec": {"behavior": {"scaleDown": {"stabilizationWindowSeconds":120}, "scaleUp": {"stabilizationWindowSeconds":120}}}, "spec": {"minReplicas":8}}'
```

maya (oncall): executing HPA patch now. will monitor autoscaler events.

ops-bot: Change ch-20260315-001 finished: flag_toggle success in 2/3 regions, eu-west-1 still rolling (replica drain in progress).

kevin (runtime): initial telemetry: p95 dropping from 1.8s -> 700ms in us-east after flip. eu-west still noisy. memory pressure down ~30%.

jonah (sre): HPA flapping reduced after stabilization window. scale events decreased, pods more stable. still seeing some 500s from old in-flight requests and cold KV misses.

priya (prod-eng): next step: follow-up hotfix to reduce continuous-batching default batch_size to 48 and add kv cache soft-limit with an LRU eviction callback. I'll open a PR but won't merge until we validate metrics baseline.

carla (support): communicated to customers: we've applied mitigation and expect recovery within 15-30 minutes. AcmeHealth appreciates proactive update.

zack (eng-infra): point of attention: autoscaler relies on CPU HPA; we should add a custom metric for kv-cache-growth to avoid mis-scaling in future. filing infra ticket.

maya (oncall): handoff: i'm going offline for 30m. jonah, kevin — you two take primary until I'm back. if anything regresses to P0, page me.

jonah (sre): ack. creating incident doc with timeline + actions: https://internal.redwood/incident/2026-03-15-kv-batch-warmup. adding perf graphs and deployment IDs.

kevin (runtime): follow-up note: root cause hypothesis -> continuous-batching warmup produced many short-lived batches with high prefix variance. KV cache warmed with many unique keys; eviction lag allowed memory working set growth and heavier compaction/kernels. Fixes: default warmup off, smaller batch caps, cache soft-limits + LRU, autoscaler metric for kv-cache-size.

priya (prod-eng): setting postmortem owner: jonah + kevin. timeline: reproduce in staging with synthetic high-prefix fanout, validate changes, propose hotfix + rollout plan next 24h.

carla (support): marking affected customers, follow-ups in #support-escalations.

ops-bot: Incident P1 -> downgraded to P2 at 2026-03-15T03:25:29Z. Reason: metrics improving and customer impact partially mitigated.

maya (oncall): back online. thanks team. leaving an action item list in the incident doc.

jonah (sre): one-liner post-incident note to include in follow-up: "Autoscaler hysteresis + cache-aware scaling would have avoided this thrash. We'll add a kv-cache metric and a 2-minute stabilization window by default."

kevin (runtime): i'll schedule a canary for the batch_size cap change and LRU cache in staging later today. will post validation checklist.

maya (oncall): closing thread to avoid noise. please add any new findings to the incident doc. :white_check_mark:
